ChatGPT said:

I created the complete pure-C project and verified that it compiles cleanly with GCC using -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror, with no libbluetooth, BlueZ API, D-Bus, bluetoothctl, or sdptool dependency.

The implementation contains three complete paths:

  1. AG initiates pairing

    Bash
    sudo ./hfp_pair pair 11:22:33:44:55:66

    It creates the BR/EDR ACL connection, performs authentication, handles SSP/legacy pairing events, saves the resulting link key, enables encryption, then performs SDP discovery.

  2. HF initiates pairing with your AG

    Bash
    sudo ./hfp_pair listen

    It accepts incoming ACL connections and handles:

    • Link Key Request

    • Link Key Notification

    • Legacy PIN Code Request

    • SSP IO Capability Request

    • Numeric Comparison

    • Passkey Entry

    • OOB rejection when unavailable

    • Authentication Complete

    • Encryption Change

    • Disconnects

  3. Retrieve the actual HFP HF RFCOMM channel

    Bash
    sudo ./hfp_pair sdp 11:22:33:44:55:66

    This is implemented directly over an L2CAP socket to SDP PSM 0x0001. It sends a raw SDP ServiceSearchAttributeRequest for the Hands-Free service UUID 0x111E, requests attribute 0x0004 (ProtocolDescriptorList), parses the SDP Data Elements, finds the RFCOMM UUID, and extracts the real server channel. SDP is specifically the Bluetooth protocol intended to discover remote services and their characteristics. Bluetooth® Technology Website HFP defines the Hands-Free/Audio Gateway architecture that uses the Bluetooth link for its control and audio connections. Bluetooth® Technology Website

A successful outgoing run looks like:

Creating BR/EDR ACL connection to 11:22:33:44:55:66
ACL connected: 11:22:33:44:55:66 handle=0x000B
Link Key Request from 11:22:33:44:55:66: no stored key
IO Capability Request from 11:22:33:44:55:66: io=0x03 auth=0x04
Simple Pairing Complete: 11:22:33:44:55:66 status=0x00
Stored link key for 11:22:33:44:55:66 (type 0x04)
Authentication Complete handle=0x000B status=0x00
Encryption Change handle=0x000B status=0x00 enabled=1

PAIRING_OK 11:22:33:44:55:66 AUTHENTICATED=1 ENCRYPTED=1
HFP_HF_RFCOMM_CHANNEL=2

Project contents

hfp_ag_raw_pairing/
├── Makefile
├── README.md
├── bt_defs.h
├── main.c
├── pairing.c
├── pairing.h
├── sdp.c
└── sdp.h

The code defines the required Linux Bluetooth socket ABI structures and HCI constants itself rather than depending on BlueZ headers. Raw HCI event filtering is also explicitly configured so security events are received rather than relying on socket defaults.

For your headless AG, the default is:

IO capability = NoInputNoOutput
Authentication = General Bonding, MITM not required
Legacy PIN = 0000
Auto confirmation = enabled

That makes common HFP headsets/phones usable without editing the source. For an older headset:

Bash
sudo ./hfp_pair --pin 0000 pair 11:22:33:44:55:66

For a device requiring authenticated numeric comparison:

Bash
sudo ./hfp_pair \
    --io-cap display-yesno \
    --mitm \
    --no-auto-confirm \
    pair 11:22:33:44:55:66

For passkey entry:

Bash
sudo ./hfp_pair \
    --io-cap keyboard-only \
    --mitm \
    --passkey 123456 \
    pair 11:22:33:44:55:66

Link keys are persisted automatically:

# BD_ADDR LINK_KEY KEY_TYPE
11:22:33:44:55:66 00112233445566778899AABBCCDDEEFF 04

The database is created with 0600 permissions and updated through a temporary file + atomic rename. On future connections, Link Key Request is answered using that stored key rather than performing a fresh pairing.

One operational requirement matters: don't have another userspace pairing agent simultaneously controlling the same adapter. On a standard Ubuntu installation, run:

Bash
sudo systemctl stop bluetooth
cd hfp_ag_raw_pairing
make

sudo ./hfp_pair listen

The Bluetooth GAP specification defines discovery, connection, and security procedures and allows different authentication/security policies, so literally forcing every arbitrary nearby device to pair is not possible when the peer itself rejects bonding or demands security capabilities your hardware/UI cannot provide. Bluetooth® Technology Website The implementation nevertheless handles both legacy PIN and the standard SSP paths needed for practical Classic Bluetooth HFP pairing.

I compile-tested the complete source, but I cannot hardware-in-the-loop test the radio/controller-specific behavior from this environment. The next integration point in your project is straightforward: use the returned HFP_HF_RFCOMM_CHANNEL=N to open your RFCOMM control connection and then start your existing HFP SLC (AT+BRSF, CIND, CMER, etc.).
